findings.title: Member list uses an invalid non-block each helper
findings.body: The template uses {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} without the block form {{#each ...}} and without a closing {{/each}}. In Ember/Handlebars this will not render the collection (or may fail to compile), so the admin group page will not display members even though the controller/model load them.

findings.title: Group member item view template name appears wrong
findings.body: The view sets templateName to 'admin/templates/group_member'. Discourse/Ember template names are normally registered without the 'templates' segment, e.g. 'admin/group_member'. If the resolver follows that convention, this view will not find its template and each member item will render blank even if the each helper is fixed.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one for exact multiples of limit
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit, such as 50 users with limit 50, it returns 2 pages instead of 1. This allows the UI to navigate to an empty extra page.

findings.title: findMembers allows an offset equal to the total member count
findings.body: findMembers clamps offset to Math.min(user_count, offset), but the last valid offset is generally user_count - limit. Allowing offset == user_count requests an empty page. This can happen after deleting the last member on the last page or via the pagination next logic, leaving the UI showing no members.

findings.title: Group members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination values
findings.body: The members action uses params[:limit].to_i and params[:offset].to_i without validating bounds. A client can request an extremely large limit, causing a large database query and serialization, or negative limit/offset values, which can trigger database errors. This is an availability risk on an endpoint that may be accessible to non-admin users.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores invalid or whitespace-padded usernames
findings.body: add_members splits the usernames string and only adds users found by User.find_by_username. It does not strip whitespace and does not report unknown usernames. If some or all usernames are invalid, the action still returns success, so the admin UI indicates members were added when they were not.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The client sends alias_level when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected while creating a new group is discarded, and the group is created with the default alias level.

findings.title: update resets visible to false on partial updates
findings.body: update unconditionally sets group.visible based on whether params[:visible] equals 'true'. Any API client that updates only some fields, such as name, without also sending visible will unintentionally hide the group. This makes partial updates unsafe and changes the previous API behavior.

findings.title: Admin groups API contract changed without compatibility
findings.body: The previous admin groups API accepted a nested group payload, allowed usernames during create/update, and supported incremental membership changes via PATCH. The new controller expects flat parameters and separate membership endpoints. Existing clients or plugins using the old admin group API may fail or silently lose membership changes.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The automatic-group case for remove_member uses xhr :put, but the route is defined as DELETE and the successful remove_member spec uses DELETE. This test does not exercise the real HTTP verb/route and could miss routing regressions.
